distribution.signatureNotes: The detached Developer ID signature record that travels with an update pack (signature.json, or --signature <file>) is verified against this pinned public key by scripts/release/install.mjs: it must name this signing identity and team, bind the sha256 of the exact manifest bytes and the sha256 of the whole pack directory, and carry a signature that verifies with this key. The private half lives in the release keychain, never in the repository, so a checkout that cannot obtain a release signature fails closed instead of installing an unauthenticated pack. signingPublicKeySha256 is the sha256 of signingPublicKeyPem exactly as JSON decodes it (real newlines, not the escaped file text), so the pin is self-checking: `node scripts/release/sign-manifest.mjs --check-policy` fails when the pair drifts, and install.mjs refuses every record while the anchor is inconsistent. The PEM shipped in the repository is a provisioning placeholder whose private half is not held; before a signing round the release job replaces it with the Developer ID public key from the release keychain and regenerates this digest, because only that key can produce a record this anchor accepts.

installers.notes: Ships every asset from models/manifest.json inside the DMG, so dictation, local conversation, memory restart and narration work on a fresh Mac with no account, no key and no post-install download. Pack bytes are verified against the manifest pins before install (scripts/release/verify-pack.mjs).

Downloads the signed model pack once after installation, verifies it against the same manifest pins, and only then claims offline use; until that download completes the app reports the missing-asset state instead of speaking.

updates.signaturePolicy: manifest-of-record authenticity: models/manifest.json declares authenticity.requiresSignature, and scripts/release/install.mjs refuses to stage anything without a valid signature record; the trust anchor is distribution.signingPublicKeyPem above and is never read from the pack.
updates.signatureCarryForward: once a store has committed a signed version it keeps requiring one (<root>/policy.json), so an update cannot silently drop the signature
updates.notes: Updates stage an immutable version, verify every asset against the pack manifest, journal the transaction and only then flip <root>/current. A verification failure never reaches the commit stage and leaves the active version untouched; an interrupted run leaves either the previous or the committed version verifiable, and rollback restores the previously active version.
